analysis.title: Charts at Goldman Sachs 19 Oct 2026
key_insights: CBOE index put volume hit the highest daily volume on record on 16 Oct, while total put volume was the 4th-highest back to 2015.
Tech was by far the most net sold global sector last week, with the largest % de-grossing in 2 months and the largest % net selling on GS record (since 2016).
The pair trade of AI winners vs AI at risk is flat on the year, after being up almost 100% from 1 Jan through end of June.
GS panic index surged at its fastest 5-day pace in years and is nearing historic extremes (as of 15 Oct).
NDX forward P/E is back to 20.5x, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023, and only a ~1.8x premium to the S&P 500, the narrowest in nearly 10 years.
The top 10 contributors account for 68% of S&P 500 3Q earnings growth.
Consensus estimates show hyperscaler capex growth exceeding 100% y/y in the quarter cited, but GS expects the earnings boost from AI capex to fade going forward.
Energy prices and bond yields have become a key driver of equities.
ETFs saw one of the largest estimated monthly net outflows in recent years in momentum, and global leveraged technology ETF AuM declined further.
GS expects S&P 500 EPS growth to decelerate but remain solid in 2027.
Market breadth has recently plunged, and the S&P 500 ex AI has rallied as AI stocks sold off. Consumer Discretionary, weak this year, rebounded over the past week.
US large cap dominance is much higher than in Europe, meaning the US market is more concentrated.

GS expects significant data center growth acceleration in US national and key regional power markets in 2026/27. Global data center GPU power demand is expected to rise from 13,510MW in 2025 to 150,081MW in 2030 (+62% CAGR), and GS total power demand CAGR rises to 3.5% through 2030.
USD high yield spread widening has been driven by data centers and related issuers.
Mortgage rates are up more than 1pp since Feb, leaving over 90% of borrowers with rates below the current market level.
If current market rates persisted, GS sees debt-to-GDP reaching 132% by 2035, 10pp above its baseline.
GS expects the surprises from computer software and accessories, the oil shock and tariffs to ease over the next year, leaving core PCE near target.
DDR memory pricing rose +7% m/m in September and trades at a +20% premium to September contract pricing. Korean DRAM exports were up +412% y/y (+11% m/m) in August.
US L/S net leverage fell 3.2pts last week, the largest weekly decline since Liberation Day and the 4th-largest in five years.
Global active ETF AuM has reached >$1.7tn. Spending growth on experiences has accelerated in recent quarters.

GS expects S&P 500 EPS growth to decelerate but remain solid in 2027 (forecast).
GS expects the earnings boost from AI capex to fade going forward (forecast).

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects the software and accessories surprise, the oil shock and tariffs to ease, bringing core PCE near target.
More than 90% of borrowers hold rates below the market level, which discourages moving.
